newsitem.title: USA: Warm weather to follow cold blast in U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Warm weather to follow cold blast in U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Another bout of frigid weather was forecast for the U.S. Midwest Thursday night and Friday morning but temperatures should quickly rise into the 70s and 80s degrees Fahrenheit late Friday and through the weekend, meteorologists said.
"We expect it (overnight lows) will set a few records, but it should not harm the wheat and corn crops," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather.
Overnight lows may dip below freezing across the northern half of Illinois and Indiana and nearly all of Ohio.
Lows Wednesday night and Thursday morning were in the mid-30s across much of the Midwest, with lows in the high 20s in parts of South Dakota, Minnesota and northern Iowa.
Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said only soft red winter wheat that was headed would be harmed by the cold, otherwise the crops should survive the cold wave.
"If there is any (headed wheat) in the northern half of Illinois you would have some problems," he said of the cold Thursday night and early Friday.
After Friday morning the Midwest and central Plains should warm up through the weekend, before somewhat cooler weather arrives late Sunday and Monday.

"We feel pretty confident this will be the last cold weather threat in the Midwest," said Solberg of the Thursday night forecast. "Overall temperatures next week in the corn belt should be normal, with highs at least in the 70s."
Both meteorologists expect scattered showers next week, with the first batch late Sunday and early Monday and a second batch Wednesday and Thursday. Rain amounts should be an inch or less.
